transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (Head Infra), Elena Morales (Sec Eng), Tom Brooks (CTO) - LucentWorks

Summary:
Short intake to validate LucentWorks' security gating for production inference. Key topics: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML & SCIM, RBAC and org separation, audit log export and retention, KMS/BYOK options, data residency and retention windows, private control plane vs hosted trade-offs.

Topics Covered:
- Compliance evidence & timing (SOC 2 + ISO 27001)
- SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping
- KMS options: Redwood-managed vs BYOK with HSM/KMS key rotation
- Audit logs: retention, tamper-evidence, SIEM export (Splunk/Datadog)
- Data retention / deletion guarantees and egress of logs
- Private deployment: VPC peering, private control plane, on-prem options

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and this is Daniel on the technical side. Could each of you quick intros?
[00:08] Raj: Raj here, Head of Infrastructure at LucentWorks. We manage cloud infra and the inference stack decisions land with me and Tom.
[00:13] Elena: Elena, security engineer, I own compliance and app security.
[00:17] Tom: Tom, CTO, mostly listening but will chime on requirements and timeline.
[00:22] Daniel: Great. Quick agenda — we want to confirm your controls baseline and any must-haves for production. We'll try to map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:30] Raj: Our initial preference is hosted or dedicated depending on controls. For PHARMA devs we need strict encryption in motion and at rest, key separation ideally BYOK because of vendor policy.
[00:40] Elena: Also SOC 2 is required, ISO would be nice to see. We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM with at least 1 year retention, and the ability to retain longer for specific customers.
[00:52] Maya: Totally. We can share SOC 2 and ISO paperwork. For KMS we support Redwood-managed keys and BYOK with customer AWS KMS or external HSM — Daniel can go deeper.
[01:00] Daniel: Quick callout: our BYOK flow supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Bring-Your-Own-HSM using PKCS#11 or cloud HSM endpoints. Rotation policies can be customer-controlled. There are sample terraform and helm snippets we can provide.
[01:15] Elena: How does Redwood prevent key exfiltration in hosted mode? We need assurance keys never leave our control.
[01:24] Daniel: In BYOK for hosted, the master key remains in your KMS. Redwood stores only short-lived wrapping keys, and we integrate using envelope encryption. For HSM-backed keys we do one-way wrapping — the private material never lands in Redwood vaults. We'll send architecture diagrams.
[01:40] Raj: And audit logs? We need immutability or at least tamper-evident logs.
[01:46] Priya: We push all request/response metadata to an append-only service; for enterprise customers we provide log export endpoints. You can ship logs to your Splunk/Datadog/S3 bucket. We can also integrate with your SIEM via syslog or forwarders.
[02:02] Elena: What's retained in logs — full prompt/response or just metadata?
[02:07] Daniel: Default is token-level metadata and request headers. We can configure to capture full payloads for audit, but that's often opted-in due to PII concerns. You can set policy per-route to mask or redact inputs.
[02:20] Tom: We have regulated customer data; by default we can't send full prompts outside our control.
[02:25] Maya: That's expected. For Dedicated or Private you can keep full logs in your environment. Hosted we can do redaction and also route full logs into your S3/KMS so they never persist in Redwood long-term.
[02:38] Raj: SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. Need RBAC mapping, ability to scope teams to tenants, and separate billing.
[02:47] Priya: We support SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can be mapped to SCIM groups; we can restrict model access per-org and enforce token scopes. For Private deployments we also support LDAP and on-prem identity proxies.
[03:02] Elena: Can we enforce MFA via our IdP?
[03:05] Maya: Yes, MFA is enforced at the IdP level. We also support conditional access via IdP claims.
[03:11] Raj: Data residency — we need EU region for EU customers, and US-eastern for domestic. How does Redwood handle tenancy and data residency in hosted?
[03:21] Daniel: We provision regional clusters. For Hosted, you can pin your tenant to a region and we provide region-specific storage and keys. For Dedicated you get a reserved pool in your region and Private gives you full control over region and network.
[03:33] Elena: On retention — legally we need to be able to purge customer data within 30 days of request and produce a proof of deletion. Is that supported?
[03:41] Maya: We have data deletion APIs and can provide deletion certificates for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted, deletion is supported and we can produce logs showing deletion events; for additional legal guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control storage.
[03:54] Tom: Our preference is private control plane if costs and ops are reasonable. What are the gating items?
[04:00] Daniel: Primary gating: network connectivity (VPC peering, PrivateLink), KMS integration (BYOK/HSM), and SCIM/SAML flows for user onboarding. Also audit log export and retention SLA. We can prototype a private control plane in a demo environment.
[04:14] Elena: SOC 2 evidence — we need the most recent report and the list of in-scope controls. Also, do you have ISO 27001 cert? Need scope document.
[04:22] Maya: We'll attach SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate with scope. We'll redact vendor-specific things but provide the control matrix.
[04:30] Raj: What's the typical time to stand up Dedicated vs Private?
[04:33] Daniel: Dedicated we can provision in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and network; Private (customer-managed control plane) is typically 6-12 weeks due to networking, security review, and testing. On-prem will be longer.
[04:45] Elena: For audit logs, can we retain for 7 years if required? Our legal wants 7y for some studies.
[04:52] Priya: Yes, retention is configurable. For Hosted we can forward to your long-term S3 archive with encryption under your key so Redwood doesn't host the archive. For Dedicated/Private you control retention directly.
[05:05] Raj: Model access controls — can we pin models per-tenant and prevent cross-tenant cache leaks?
[05:12] Daniel: Yes, model pinning and per-tenant compute isolation exists. KV cache is namespaced by tenant and by deployment; we have guardrails to prevent cross-tenant cache leakage. We'll include the technical note about cache isolation and the sequence-length behavior.
[05:27] Elena: Any FedRAMP or health-care specific certifications?
[05:30] Maya: Not FedRAMP currently; for healthcare we support BAA conversations and can provide additional controls in Private deployments. We'll flag compliance gaps and mitigations in the security pack.
[05:40] Tom: What about pen test reports or VAPT?
[05:43] Maya: We can share summary VAPT results and remediation tracker; for detailed reports we require an NDA.
[05:49] Raj: Encryption at rest — is data encrypted with customer keys or Redwood keys?
[05:53] Daniel: By default Redwood-managed keys are used. For Dedicated and Hosted with BYOK, data at rest is encrypted under customer KMS. For Private you can bring your own KMS and control everything.
[06:03] Elena: How are secrets handled for model artifacts and container images?
[06:07] Priya: Images are pulled from registries over mTLS and secrets are injected at runtime with vault-backed ephemeral secrets. Artifacts are stored in encrypted object stores with access policies.
[06:19] Tom: Ok, rough timeline — we want pilot within Q2, production by Q3 if gating is ok. Is that feasible?
[06:27] Daniel: Feasible. Next step is to run through a lightweight pilot: private control plane demo, KMS integration test, and log export validation. We'll need your infra folks to enable VPC peering and provide test keys.
[06:40] Elena: We will also run an internal legal review; please send all certs/docs.
[06:44] Maya: Absolutely. We'll send a package with SOC2, ISO cert, VAPT summary, and the BYOK integration guide. Also will include sample terraform and helm snippets for Private deploy.
[06:55] Raj: Can you provide an estimated cost delta between Hosted with BYOK and Dedicated?
[06:59] Samir: We'll provide a high-level delta sheet; Hosted with BYOK is generally lower monthly cost but less isolation; Dedicated adds reserved GPU capacity and higher cost but gives stronger isolation and control. We'll send numbers.
[07:12] Tom: One last question — audit log tamper evidence, do you support append-only WORM buckets or signed log chains?
[07:18] Daniel: We support forwarding to WORM-enabled S3 and can provide signed log digests (merkle-tree style summaries) on request for high-assurance customers.
[07:29] Elena: That would satisfy legal in many cases.
[07:32] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps then.
[07:35] Maya (recap): Action items: Maya to send compliance pack + network diagram; Daniel to prepare BYOK/HSM options and sample config; Elena to send retention policy and legal contact; schedule SE workshop for private control plane next week.
[07:50] Raj: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:53] Tom: Thanks.
[07:55] Maya: We'll follow up by email with links to docs and propose times for the workshop.

Notes & references mentioned:
- SOC 2 Type II report (to be sent)
- ISO 27001 cert and scope (to be sent)
- BYOK/HSM integration guide (samples: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, PKCS#11)
- Sample terraform/helm snippets for Private control plane
- VAPT summary (NDA for full report)
- Log export options: Splunk/Datadog/S3 + WORM buckets and signed digests

End of transcript.
